meta.title: ShramkoGSFPV — FPV drone simulator for real 3D scans, in your browser
meta.description: Free, open-source FPV simulator in your browser: fly 1,300+ real Gaussian Splatting scans from SuperSplat, shrink to fly a room like a city, crash into real walls, use your radio over USB. No install.
meta.ogTitle: Fly an FPV drone through real 3D scans — right in your browser

hero.h1: Fly an FPV drone through real 3D scans — right in your browser
hero.sub: ShramkoGSFPV turns 1,300+ Gaussian Splatting scans from SuperSplat into places you can fly: real rooms, streets and gardens with walls you actually crash into, Betaflight-style rates and PID, and your own radio over USB or touch sticks. Nothing to install.
hero.ctaNote: Works best in desktop Chrome or Edge with WebGPU.

how.h2: Three steps from a scan to the air
how.lead: No account, no download. The scene streams straight from SuperSplat into your browser.

steps.d: Pick one of 1,300+ walkable scans in the simulator's SuperSplat tab, one of Andrii's, or paste the link to any public SuperSplat scene.
Plug in an EdgeTX radio in USB joystick mode (WebHID), use a gamepad, or fly with touch sticks.
Move the sticks once to calibrate, arm with the throttle all the way down — like a real quad — and go.

real.h2: A quad that behaves like the one in your hands
real.lead: An own flight model — four motors, a mixer and a rate PID — flying inside the real geometry of the scan.

items.d: Every physics tick sweeps the drone's body against the scan's voxel collision data, so a fast quad can't slip through a thin wall between frames.
Hit something hard and the quad tumbles and throws debris. Brush a wall gently and it slides along it.
Betaflight, Actual, KISS and Raceflight rate curves match Betaflight 4.5.1's own code with 0 error at 1880 points, both computed in double precision (in float32 they differ by at most 0.00063 °/s).
Flights are recorded as stick input and replay deterministically: the same inputs always give the same flight.
Earth, Moon, Mars or zero-g. On the Moon the same drone gets extremely twitchy — the “keep thrust-to-weight” switch tames it.

mode.label: Flight mode
mode.help: Angle levels the drone when you let go of the sticks; Horizon levels it too but flips at full stick; Acro holds the attitude, like a freestyle quad.

angleLimitDeg.label: Angle mode tilt limit
angleLimitDeg.help: The steepest tilt Angle mode allows, as Betaflight's angle limit.

strength.label: Self-levelling strength
strength.help: How hard Angle mode pulls the drone back to level, as Betaflight's level strength.

horizonStrength.label: Horizon levelling strength
horizonStrength.help: How hard Horizon mode levels the drone near the stick centre.

enabled.label: Crashes
enabled.help: Off: hitting a wall never ends the flight, so a beginner can keep flying.

vCrash.label: Crash threshold
vCrash.help: Impact speed above which a hit counts as a crash; slower touches slide along the wall.

gravity.label: Gravity
gravity.help: Earth 9.81, Moon 1.62, Mars 3.72, zero-g, or any value in between.

gravityMode.label: Thrust on other worlds
gravityMode.help: Same motors (honest), the thrust-to-weight you have on Earth, or auto throttle that hovers at stick centre.

twr.label: Thrust-to-weight
twr.help: Maximum thrust divided by weight; the preset takes it from the manufacturer or an estimate.

tauMs.label: Motor spin-up time
tauMs.help: How fast the motors reach a new speed; lower feels snappier.

dragScale.label: Air drag
dragScale.help: Scales the air drag of the frame: more drag slows the drone down sooner.

ductDrag.label: Duct drag
ductDrag.help: Rotor and duct drag that damps a cinewhoop's speed and wobble.

propInertia.label: Propeller inertia
propInertia.help: Scales the spin inertia of the props: more inertia softens throttle and turns.

idlePct.label: Motor idle
idlePct.help: Motor speed at zero throttle, like Betaflight's DShot idle value.

auto.label: Automatic respawn
auto.help: After a crash the drone is back in the air by itself.

delayS.label: Respawn delay
delayS.help: How long the crash stays on screen before the automatic respawn.

target.label: Respawn at
target.help: Rewind to where you were a few seconds before the crash, or go back to the start.

rewindS.label: Rewind by
rewindS.help: How many seconds before the crash the rewind puts you back.

platform.label: Respawn on a platform
platform.help: You restart hovering on an invisible pad instead of dropping to the floor.

keepArmed.label: Stay armed after a respawn
keepArmed.help: No need to flip the arm switch again after every crash.

unstuck.label: Get unstuck automatically
unstuck.help: Restarts the flight when the drone is stuck or lies upside down.

showPad.label: Show the platform
showPad.help: Draws the respawn pad, which is invisible by default.

refill.label: Battery refill
refill.help: When the simulated pack is full again: at the start, at every respawn, or never.

fovDeg.label: Camera field of view
fovDeg.help: How wide the FPV camera sees; each drone keeps its own value.

uptiltDeg.label: Camera uptilt
uptiltDeg.help: How far the FPV camera tilts up; more tilt suits faster flying.

hud.label: Show HUD
hud.help: The on-screen display: arm state, flight mode, battery, speed and altitude.

units.label: Units
units.help: Metric or imperial units on the HUD and in the flight stats.

quality.label: Stable frame ↔ detail
quality.help: Moves the render resolution and detail budget. Physics always runs at 1000 Hz.

governor.label: Automatic quality
governor.help: Lowers the quality by itself when frames drop, and raises it again when the GPU has room.

reducedMotion.label: Reduced motion
reducedMotion.help: A calmer crash camera without flashes; follows your system setting by default.

frameStats.label: Frame stats
frameStats.help: Screen refresh, frame times and input-to-screen delay over the flight view.

onDisarm.label: Flight stats on disarm
onDisarm.help: Shows the flight's stats card, like the goggles' OSD, when you disarm.

language.label: Language
language.help: English, Spanish, Polish or Russian; by default the language of the page.

stickMode.label: Stick mode
stickMode.help: Which stick is the throttle in the calibration drawings: Mode 2 on the left, Mode 1 on the right.

current.label: Drone
current.help: One of the BetaFPV-class presets; every number on its card says where it comes from.

pid.label: PID gains (P / I / D / F)
pid.help: P, I, D and feed-forward for roll, pitch and yaw, per drone, as in Betaflight.

rates.label: Rates (stick curves)
rates.help: Betaflight, Actual, KISS or Raceflight rate curves, imported from your Betaflight CLI diff.

throttle.label: Throttle curve
throttle.help: Throttle mid and expo from your Betaflight diff.

autoSwitch.label: Next scene after a crash
autoSwitch.help: After a crash, carry on in the next scene of your rotation; off by default.

rotation.label: Scene rotation
rotation.help: Which scenes the next and the random scene come from.

allowNoWalls.label: Include scans without walls
allowNoWalls.help: Lets the rotation pick scans that have no collision data.

transform.label: Scene size
transform.help: Scales a wrong-size scan around the drone, remembered for each scene.

dropFloaters.label: Remove floating pieces
dropFloaters.help: Removes floating voxel pieces smaller than this many blocks (phantom walls), for each scene.

show.label: Voxel grid
show.help: Shows the collision voxels over the scan, or only the voxels with the scan hidden.

opacity.label: Voxel opacity
opacity.help: How see-through the voxel grid is.

style.label: Voxel style
style.help: Solid cubes, a grid, edges, height colours, or floating pieces in red.

radiusM.label: Voxel radius
radiusM.help: How far around the drone the grid is drawn.

fps.label: Recording frame rate
fps.help: 30 or 60 frames per second in the saved video.

resolution.label: Recording resolution

locations.h2: Every walkable scan on SuperSplat is now a place to fly: 1,300+ and growing
locations.lead: Real rooms, gardens, streets and churches, scanned by people around the world and published with walls you crash into. Let the simulator pick, change places on every crash, or bring your own scan.

items.d: The SuperSplat tab in the simulator lists every public scan with walls, with superspl.at's own sorting, filters and search.

items.t: A new place after every crash
items.d: Star the scans you like, switch on “Next scene after a crash”, and every crash drops you somewhere else, in random order: your favourites, the places you have flown or Andrii's picks.
N: next scene, Shift+N: random, Shift+F: next favourite. The page does not reload and your radio stays connected.
Publish a scan on SuperSplat, or take any public one, and paste its link here or in the simulator.

scale.h2: Shrink yourself: fly a room like a city
scale.lead: Two keys scale the whole scene around the drone, from ×0.25 to ×100. At ×100 you are the size of a mosquito: a chair is a tower block, the gap under the bed a canyon. Dive along a chair leg — it is an awesome feeling.
scale.macro: Macro scans work too: a plant, a toy or an insect is a small real object, so scale it up from ×3 to ×10 and fly it like a big building, among the leaves or around a fly. Such scenes can start already enlarged, and [ and ] change the size at any moment. The other way round, shrink a city (down to ×0.25) so it feels like a model, and fly it with a micro whoop.

stops.d: a scan that came out too big

steps: Open a room: Andrii's villa, the winter garden or any indoor scan.
Hold ] to grow the scene ([ shrinks it, Shift+] doubles it at once), or drag Scene size in the pause menu. Each scan keeps its own scale.
The walls grow with it, so you still crash into the chair leg you dive past.

risks.lead: Short and honest, so nothing catches you by surprise.

items.t: Scene data can change without notice
items.d: Scenes load from SuperSplat's public but undocumented CDN. It can change at any time, and some scenes may stop loading.

items.t: Some scans come without collision data
items.d: For those, the simulator can build walls right in your browser with SuperSplat’s own tool (up to 4 million Gaussians, about 25 seconds for a 2.1-million scan on a desktop GPU). Bigger scans stay fly-through.

Crashes and fast flight can make you queasy, so take breaks. Measured over 50 crashes, effects flash at most 2 times per second, under the WCAG limit of 3; your reduced-motion setting is respected (not tested yet).

items.t: A simulator is not a real flight
items.d: Practise responsibly, follow your local drone law and never fly over people.
Calibration, flight history and favourites are stored only in your browser.

items.q: How can I fly an FPV drone through a 3D Gaussian Splatting scan?
items.a: Open ShramkoGSFPV in desktop Chrome or Edge, pick a scan (1,300+ with walls in the SuperSplat tab, one of Andrii's or a pasted SuperSplat link), connect a radio, a gamepad or touch sticks, then calibrate, arm and fly. There is nothing to install.

items.q: Can I use my RadioMaster radio in the browser?
items.a: That is what it is built for: switch an EdgeTX radio such as the TX16S, Boxer, Pocket or Zorro to USB joystick mode and connect it over WebHID in Chrome or Edge. So far this has been tested only in Chrome with a simulated EdgeTX radio, not with real hardware or in Edge.

items.q: Is there a free FPV simulator that runs in the browser?
items.a: Yes. ShramkoGSFPV is free and open source under the MIT license. It runs on WebGPU in desktop Chrome or Edge, with no download.

items.q: Which SuperSplat scenes can I fly?
items.a: Any public SuperSplat scene, by link or id; the simulator's SuperSplat tab lists the 1,300+ published with walls, with superspl.at's own filters. Those have solid walls at once; for the others you can build walls in your browser with one click (scans up to 4 million Gaussians). Bigger scans can be flown through but not crashed into.

items.q: Does it work on iPad or phone?
items.a: Touch sticks have been tested only in desktop Chrome's touch emulation, not in Safari, on iPad or in Android browsers yet, and you need a browser with WebGPU. Radios need desktop Chrome or Edge.

items.q: Is the flight physics like Betaflight?
items.a: The rate curves (Betaflight, Actual, KISS, Raceflight) match Betaflight 4.5.1's own code with 0 error at 1880 points when both are computed in double precision, and a rate PID drives four motors through a mixer. It is our own flight model, not Betaflight firmware.

items.q: Do I crash into walls or fly through them?
items.a: On scenes with collision data you crash: the drone's body is swept against the voxel data on every physics tick, and a test harness checks that fast flight cannot tunnel through walls. See Live numbers for the result.
Yes, MIT. Code, measurements and design decisions are on GitHub. Betaflight's formulas were re-implemented; no GPL code was copied.

items.q: Can the simulator take me to a new place after every crash?
items.a: Yes. Random top-rated in the SuperSplat tab opens a scan you have not seen, Shift+N loads a random scene in flight, and with “Next scene after a crash” switched on every crash takes you to another scene: from Andrii's picks, your favourites or the scenes you have flown, in random or fixed order. The radio stays connected.

items.q: Can I fly a room as if it were a city?
items.a: Yes. Scene size scales the whole scan around the drone from ×0.25 to ×100 with [ and ] (Shift+] doubles it) or in the pause menu. At ×100 a chair is the size of a tower block and you can dive along its legs; the walls scale with the scene, so you still crash into them. The scale is kept for each scan.

items.q: Can I fly my own 3D scan?
items.a: Yes. Publish it on SuperSplat (superspl.at) and paste its link or id on this page or in the simulator. Published with walls (voxel collision data), it is solid at once; without them you can build walls in the browser for scans up to 4 million Gaussians.

items.q: Can I help make a simulator drone fly like my real one, or ask for a new drone?
items.a: Yes. The drones are built from published numbers and estimates: BetaFPV-class whoops, an iFlight Nazgul Evoque F5 class 5-inch freestyle quad, a Mach R5 Sport class 5-inch race quad and a Taurus X8 class cinelifter carrying a RED Komodo. If you fly one of them for real and it feels different, press Help tune it in the drone picker or in Settings and send your Betaflight diff all, a link to a blackbox log and a few words; Andrii fits the drone to it. The same form asks for a drone that is not in the list.

tour.lead: Every picture on this page is a real screenshot of the live simulator: {n} of them, taken on {date} by a script in the repository, so they can be taken again after every release.
rows: Plug in an EdgeTX radio and a drawn radio walks you through it: stick by stick, then the switch you arm with, then a check of every channel before you fly. Each step waits until you really move the stick.

Angle self-levelling by default for everyone; the chip on screen, M or a switch on your radio picks Horizon or Acro. No radio at hand? The keyboard shows every key it uses, touch sticks appear on a touch screen, and a gamepad connects through the browser (not tested on real hardware yet).

BetaFPV-class whoops, a 5-inch freestyle and a 5-inch race quad and an X8 cinelifter with a cinema camera, and every number on their cards says where it comes from. Paste a Betaflight CLI diff to fly with your own rates and PID.

Hit a wall and the quad crashes at the speed it hit, the wreck tumbling with debris; two seconds later it is back in the air, 5 s back along your path and still armed. Crashes off, the delay and where you come back sit in Settings.

An OSD like in your goggles, field of view and camera uptilt. F9 records 60 fps video of Andrii's scans with their credit in the picture, auto-record catches every flight into your folder, and a flight log becomes a 60 fps video up to 4K.

Pick one of 1,300+ walkable scans in the SuperSplat tab with its own filters, one of Andrii's, or paste a link, and watch it load with real numbers. N, Shift+N and Shift+F change the scene in the page with the radio still connected; [ and ] scale the scene from ×0.25 to ×100.

Show the walls you crash into as a voxel grid over the scan, or fly the grid alone. A noisy scan? Drop its floating specks, the phantom walls, with a live preview, or switch the walls off for every scene.

Every setting on one screen, kept between visits, with export, import and reset. Disarm and a goggles-style card shows the flight; pause and the summary panel has its stats, every menu item and every key.

privacy.title: Privacy — ShramkoGSFPV
privacy.description: What ShramkoGSFPV collects, why, for how long, and your rights under the GDPR.

p: The controller of your data is Andrii Shramko. You can reach him at zmei116@gmail.com or through the contact form on this site.

The site and the simulator send a few whitelisted events to their own server at /api/e: page views (only the language of the page), switching language, clicks on the main buttons and contact links, opening and switching a scene, the kind of input connected (radio, gamepad, keyboard or touch), arming, crashes and the walls switch. No cookies are set, no device identifier is created and the events do not contain your IP address.
Purpose: understanding which parts of the site and the simulator are useful (legitimate interest, Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). Events are kept for 12 months.

sections.h: Google Analytics — only with your consent
p: The site and the simulator use Google Analytics 4, a service of Google Ireland Limited (Gordon House, Barrow Street, Dublin 4, Ireland), only if you press Accept in the banner. Until then nothing from Google is loaded. Consent mode starts with every storage type denied, and Accept grants analytics storage only; advertising features and Google signals are off.

After you accept, Google Analytics sets the cookies _ga and _ga_E7X0ES0QBE on this site and records the pages you view and what you do on them: the events of the counter above, the sections of the page you scroll to, the forms you start and send (never their content or your e-mail address) and errors of the page's scripts, together with your browser, device type and an approximate location that Google derives from your IP address (Google Analytics 4 does not store the IP address). The cookies expire after 14 months at most, and Google keeps this data for 14 months; it may be processed outside the EU under the EU standard contractual clauses.

Legal basis: your consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR). Your choice is kept in your browser's storage. You can withdraw it at any time: Cookie settings at the bottom of every page (in the simulator: Cookie settings in the pause menu), then Decline. The cookies are then deleted and nothing more is sent to Google.
Radio calibration, flight history and favourites stay in your browser's storage. They are strictly necessary for the simulator to work, never leave your device and need no consent.
If you send the form, your email, the role you chose and your message are stored on the server and forwarded to the owner's Telegram notification bot.
They are kept until your request is handled or until you ask for them to be deleted. Legal basis: your consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR).

If you send a bug report or an idea from the simulator or this site, your message, the page and scene you were on, the release, your language and, if you leave one, your contact (an e-mail address or another handle) are stored on the server. Technical details (browser, graphics card, screen, frame times, recent errors, settings, the flight log and a small picture of the view) are added only if you tick the box for them.

A Drone physics report, sent with Help tune it in the simulator, also carries the drone it is about, the Betaflight text and the blackbox log link you paste and, unless you untick its box, the simulator settings you changed for that drone, the flight mode and the input you fly with (radio, gamepad, keyboard or touch). They are stored and forwarded like a bug's technical details.

Everything you send, including your message, your contact and, if you added them, the technical details and the picture, is forwarded to the owner's Telegram chat (so it passes through Telegram's servers), where he reads and sorts the reports. Your e-mail address is used only to answer you: the owner's replies, and a thank-you once your idea is in the simulator, come from his Gmail address (zmei116@gmail.com) through Google's mail servers. So that a reply reaches you in the language you wrote in, your message (to recognise its language) and the owner's reply (to translate it) are sent to Google's Gemini API. Nothing is sent automatically, and if you reply, your answer goes to his Gmail inbox. If you tell him an idea in person and give him your address, it is kept and used the same way.

Reports are kept while the idea or the problem is being worked on and afterwards as a record of how the simulator was improved. The public roadmap shows only titles written by us, never your words or your contact. You can ask at any time for your report, or only your e-mail address, to be deleted. Legal basis: your consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR), given by sending the report and ticking the box for technical details.

Scene preview images on this page, and the scenes themselves in the simulator, are loaded by your browser directly from PlayCanvas servers (SuperSplat). As with any website, those servers see your IP address.

You can ask for access to your data, its correction or erasure, restriction of processing, data portability, and you can object to processing or withdraw consent — through the contact form or by email.
You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the Polish supervisory authority, the President of the Personal Data Protection Office (UODO).
